speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth in respect of the Auditor-General's Report for FY2017/2018 (a) how much additional costs were hidden in the award of contracts to the overseas tenderer for the Mid-Autumn Festival 2016 and Chinese New Year 2017; (b) whether there were such similar hidden costs paid to this overseas tenderer from 2014 to 2016 and how much was it in total; (c) what independent investigations had been carried out to address the telltale signs that the reimbursement claims made by the People's Association (PA) officer for overseas purchases for use in Chingay Parade 2017 might not be authentic; and (d) whether any of the statutory auditors of PA in previous audits flagged out such lapses since 2013.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: Instead, AGO pointed out that the successful tenderer had in its tender proposal required the organiser to bear additional obligations, which included transportation charges and provision of a site for lantern-assembly.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: The AGO had flagged this as an administrative lapse because the organiser did not take into consideration these costs in its tender evaluation for price comparison.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: The organiser has acknowledged the lapse and put in place measures to avoid its recurrence.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: While there was no conclusive evidence that there was wrongdoing, there were concerns over the authenticity of some transactions.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: We will decide on further steps after the Police complete their investigations.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: Mr Png Eng Huat asked if any of these lapses were flagged out in the past by statutory auditors.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: The AGO observations for the Mid-Autumn Festival, Chinese New Year and Chingay events were not observed in past external audits conducted.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: PA immediately stopped these practices for Chingay in early 2017, even before AGO's recent audit.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: We will continue to educate our staff and volunteers to improve the procurement practices.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: We will also review the rules for local and overseas purchases with a view of simplifying them for ease of application and compliance.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: Procedures adopted by PA must be simple, robust but not overly onerous on the staff and the large number of volunteers to adhere to.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: We will continue to balance the need for agility and accountability.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, I thank the Minister for the answer.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I just got a couple of supplementary questions.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Who should be ultimately held accountable for such lapses – the grassroots organisations volunteers or the management of PA?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Because the PA is not run by volunteers, it is headed by People's Action Party Ministers and Members of Parliament in this Chamber and it is allocated a huge budget, closing in on $1 billion with professionally paid staff, so it is not an amateur outfit to begin with.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister where the buck stops for accountability at PA.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The second question is: does the Minister agree that the work of the current auditor for PA, which has been giving PA a clean report since financial year (FY) 2013, needs to be audited as it could not pick up serious lapses repeatedly, some with telltale signs of possible fraud as reported in the AGO report?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: And since there is no assurance that the audit work at PA was done to the highest standard of transparency and corporate governance, would the Minister consider ordering an independent investigation or a full AGO audit, or even a forensic audit to ensure public money is well spent?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The last question is: does the Minister agree that it is important to hold PA to greater accountability going forward, since the weakness at PA has not been addressed over time and the lapses have become more brazen?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And that has been the way the Government operates before, now and in the future.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It has not changed and it will not change.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We do a thorough investigation on every lapse, small or big, and we take responsibility for every mistake made and we put them right.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Second, the Member alleged that there are serious lapses and fraud.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: If we look at the AGO report, the AGO has done their job professionally, unless the Member is suggesting that the AGO has not done its job professionally.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I do not think that AGO used those words.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I think it is not appropriate for us to put words into the AGO's mouth unless you are making a separate serious allegation, which we will take up seriously.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I have no doubt on the integrity of my public officers and their professionalism.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I accept that sometimes they make mistakes and, when they do, we will put it right.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But please do not use words that do not correspond to the reality or words that the AGO has not used.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is quite different from other cases which Mr Png may be familiar with.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: There is a material difference between whether an audit report is qualified and not qualified.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Audit reports will always find in most, if not all, cases, some areas for improvements, and some areas where mistakes need to be rectified.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But there is a material difference whether a set of accounts is qualified or not qualified.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And I think Mr Png knows the difference.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Because it goes to the heart of whether the accounts can be accepted by the public or not.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: PA is a large organisation run by professional staff as well as an even larger group of volunteers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is not an excuse for PA to make mistakes.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We are fully aware of the nature of PA's work.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We are also fully aware of the type of work that the PA needs to do.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: A large volunteer base, which is why we constantly simplify our rules to make sure that the rules are compliant with processes and yet easily adhered to.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We continuously find a balance between the two: the need for accountability and agility.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, I think it would not be right for us to insinuate that the public officers and, least of all, that the AGO has not done a proper work.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: If there is a suspicion that the AGO has not done a proper work, we will take the AGO to task.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The AGO is independent in its report and it will stay so.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, I want to remind Mr Png, first, there is a serious difference between what we call a report whereby the auditors have a disclaimer of opinion where they are not able to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence to provide a basis for an audit opinion.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: AGO has consistently given the Government an unmodified audit opinion – unmodified audit opinion – on its financial statements.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This means that the Government's financial statements containing the accounts of all Ministries, departments and Organs of State are reliable and public funds are properly accounted for.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Similarly, Statutory Boards have received unmodified audit opinions from their respective auditors in their recent audit.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Now, this is a material difference between a qualified set of accounts and a set of accounts that have no such qualification.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In PA, some of the mistakes made were found by our own internal processes and we made it right even before AGO comes.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We reviewed the processes, we tightened the processes, we cooperated fully with the investigators to put things right.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And when there is wrongdoing, we own up to it and we put it right.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I think the public can make their own assessment as to the difference between how we handle our audit very seriously and how others handle theirs.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Deputy Speaker, the AGO report actually mentioned that there were serious weaknesses in control and there were telltale signs that certain documents were not authentic.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: AGO will not use such words unless there is reasonable doubt.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: I think I spoke in this Parliament before that AGO did a special audit on AHPETC and I accepted all the findings.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: In terms of audit report, the PA has many years of qualified accounts.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Minister Chan, are you raising a point of order?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I do not think that is what the AGO said.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Adverse opinion is the worst opinion they can ever get for an audit report; six consecutive years.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: And I have asked why then there is no independent audit on PA.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: And then, when it finally cleared its accounts in 2013, every year is, I think, true and fair.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: And when AGO audited it in 2014, 2017, they found all these serious lapses.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: So, what I am asking for is accountability.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Accountability must mean something, it must mean for all.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: And it is not too much to ask for that.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Can I have a confirmation that the Member is not questioning the integrity of our AGO?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I have similar respect for my AGO's work.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And if that is so, then we take the AGO report as what it is.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And I would like to repeat this: there is a material difference to what it means by a set of qualified accounts and what it means not to have that qualification.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I think we are very clear in our mind whether the PA accounts were qualified or not.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I suggest the Member invite Mr Chen Show Mao, who is sitting beside him, who is well-versed in this, to clarify what is the difference between a set of qualified accounts and otherwise.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The comments refer to specifically this: should the whole set of things be put under the tender or this part we put under tender and the cost, the other portion of the cost that have to be borne, because of the transportation and the storage, be combined together?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That is the clarification I want to make.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, it is not that the costs have not been accounted for.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is not as if there are no bills and receipts to justify the payment.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is not that there is anything that has not been shown to the public or revealed to the auditors.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: I think just now the Minister said that because of the auditor giving us a qualified account for two years – I think the history is there, it had been debated here – because of that, the Government ordered AGO to audit our accounts, because our auditor qualified our accounts.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Then, I would like to ask the Minister, PA has many years of qualified accounts before 2007 and six years of consecutive adverse report, why then did the Government not order any audits on PA?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As a layman, let me try again to explain in layman's terms.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In every audit report, we can expect to find mistakes made, no excuse.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Having made mistakes, does it mean that the set of accounts can be trusted, in layman's term?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: If the set of accounts can be trusted, because notwithstanding the mistakes made, that means there is no material impact, then we do not need to have a qualified opinion.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But if the auditor comes out and say that, "I look at the set of accounts, yes, there are mistakes made, but on top of the mistakes made, I cannot be confident that this set of accounts is correct and can be trusted." Then, people will give a qualified opinion.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And I am not sure that the Member's statement is correct: that PA has a qualified set of accounts.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: PA has made mistakes, we accept, we acknowledge and we will rectify and put it right.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But at no time was it ever suggested that the accounts cannot be trusted; that there is a material impact that the set of accounts cannot be trusted.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: If the Member likes, I would clarify the following things.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I know that the Member has been trying to draw a comparison between Aljunied-Hougang Town Council's (AHTC's) case and PA's, and AGO's findings for various Government agencies.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As the AHTC's lawsuit is pending before the Courts, I will limit my comments to what is material.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Any lapses in Government agencies can undermine public confidence in the Government as an institution and affects the integrity of our Civil Service.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And this is why it is necessary, in the public interest, to explain and distinguish the facts, circumstances and follow-up actions concerning the AHTC's lapse and those found by the AGO in the Government agencies.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And I will limit myself to the facts.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The issues surrounding AHTC's case are very different from the lapses found by AGO in Government agencies.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This means that the Government's financial statements containing the accounts of all Ministries, departments and Organs of States are reliable and public funds are probably accounted for.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But that does not mean that there are no mistakes.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Similarly, Statutory Boards have received unmodified audit opinions from their respective auditors in their recent audits.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The Government has rules and procedures in place to ensure proper systems of checks and balances.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: AGO audits pointed out that the instances of lapses found in the Government agencies were failure to comply with these rules.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: These lapses were taken in the context of a much larger Public Service with more than 140,000 officers handling hundreds and thousands of transactions every year.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The difference is this: our rules are in place.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: When compliance is not in order, we take officers to task and we improve and tighten up the system.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Third, on the Government agencies' response to lapses found by AGO, their responses have been to take firm action against individuals responsible.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And if I may add, even before AGO comes in, various of the agencies have their own internal audits, just like PA, to pick out mistakes made and to rectify them ahead of time.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Where criminal offence is suspected, the cases are promptly surfaced to the Head of Department or organisation and a report filed with the relevant authority, such as the Police or the Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau, and this is exactly what has happened.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: To give an example, following the AGO's audit report indicating possible wrongdoings in relation to the procurement in the National Library Board in 2014, we referred the case to the Police and a former officer has been charged for corruption.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: There are other past criminal cases reported in the media.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We do not hide them, we do not sweep them under the carpet.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We face them squarely and we take the actions necessary.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For administrative and procedural lapses, disciplinary actions are taken against officers where warranted.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: These range from counselling and warning to stoppage of salary increment and dismissal.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Government agencies take AGO's audit observations very seriously and are committed to rectifying the lapses.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Where there are lapses, they will openly acknowledge and steps are taken to address them as soon as possible and lessons are shared across the entire Public Service.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Government agencies are accountable to the Public Accounts Committee for their corrective and preventive actions taken in response to these lapses.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Last, I wish to clarify a key point.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The lawsuit was instituted in the name of AHTC by an independent panel.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, to conclude, it is wrong to compare the problem surfaced by auditors of AHTC to lapses by public sector agencies identified in AGO's reports.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: There are proper rules and procedures in place to ensure checks and balances and, where lapses are found, agencies are prompt in closing the gaps and holding individuals to account.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In all these, we do not make light of any mistakes made.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We run a clean system and we have every intention to run a clean and open system.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The fact that we run a large system with many volunteers does not excuse us from making mistakes.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But when we make mistakes, we found out, we tighten the process, we improve.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We do not shirk our responsibilities or try to diminish the mistake by comparing with other people who have made other mistakes.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We put in place our processes to check ourselves ahead of time, even before other people come and check us.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And when other people come and check us, we work with them transparently, openly and to improve our system.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: When mistakes are made, we take the necessary actions to put the system right and to punish any wrongdoing.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And I think the public can have every confidence that this Government takes our responsibilities seriously and transparently.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We owe it to ourselves, we owe it to our nation that we abide by the highest standard in our duties to our Ministries, organisations, but, most importantly, to our people and country.
